engagement_title: Ada Hollis wall and Thanksgiving folio: bring nine home scans of one woman to a single archive, rebuild the retired framer's caption cards from the file that went to press, and hand back the print set, the folio and the wall plan
vertical: Media, publishing and personal: heritage photograph restoration commissioned privately by a family (Vermont, New England)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com posting 'Old Picture Restoration' (30 to 250 USD), whose client writes 'I need a physical photo restored. This is a personal keepsake and means a lot to me.' and lists 'Restore colors, details, and sharpness.' plus 'Experience with color correction and detail enhancement.' Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com brief from an individual with several old photo scans to restore 'for A4 printing to mount on my wall', naming colour fading as the damage. The killed spec sat on one surface and leaned on scratch and tear repair, which is generative healing and does not exist here; it was also a single atomic grade. The fuller commission this family genuinely has is the whole wall: the restoration, the framer's caption cards (a true record per page run rebuildable from the press file he left behind), and the keepsake folio they will keep editing after we go. Names, town and family are invented for this benchmark.
client_one_liner: Nine scans of our grandmother from nineteen twelve to nineteen seventy four, faded and crooked and not looking like the same person, and twenty two of us come back to the house at Thanksgiving to hang a wall of her.
client_brief:
Hollis family: Ada's wall, and the folio for Thanksgiving

Our grandmother Ada Hollis died in April at ninety nine. Twenty two of us come back to the house in Vermont at Thanksgiving, and we want to hang a wall of her, properly framed, and give every grandchild a folio to take home.

What we have is nine photographs, scanned at home on a flatbed by my brother, covering roughly nineteen twelve to nineteen seventy four. Some are studio card portraits, some are drugstore colour prints from the sixties and seventies that have gone a strange colour, and a couple are crooked. Laid next to each other they do not look like they belong to the same wall, let alone the same person.

We want them brought back to something we would be proud to frame, and we want them to hang together. Correct the fading, the colour and the tilt. Do not invent anything. Ada had a scar on her left hand from a stove, and a reprint somebody paid for in the eighties took it out, and my mother has never forgiven it. Whatever is really in the photograph stays in the photograph.

We need the print files for framing, smaller versions we can send around the family, and one caption card for each photograph, the way the framer in Brattleboro used to make them. He shut last year. We only have the file he sent to press for the 2019 set, and the new cards have to match those, because six of them are already on the wall.

We also want the folio: a cover, the photographs with what we know about each, and a page showing how the wall is laid out. Make it something we can change ourselves, because my aunt will find three more names.

Finally, tell us what you corrected and what you deliberately left alone, and why.

Quiet, please. Like a museum, not a memory book.
price_band_and_audience: A private heritage commission of 650 to 1,600 dollars, paid by three siblings in their sixties on behalf of twenty two family members aged 8 to 74, hung in a family house rather than sold to anyone. The band is load-bearing in an unusual direction: the money buys restraint, not effect. At this band the correct answer is a true archival neutral, deep honest blacks, one photograph per folio page, generous margins, a caption voice that reads like a museum label, and visible respect for the grain and the paper the print is actually made of. The same brief bought for 60 dollars from an online memory book service would correctly be warmer, brighter, collaged full bleed, set in a script face with drop shadows and a heart on the cover, and shipping that here is a failure the family will feel personally rather than commercially. Pushed the other way into a heavy sepia wash or a gallery black ground it becomes a stranger's idea of an old photograph, which is the other way to lose this job. Anything that reads as enhanced fails regardless of execution.

brand_identity.sector: A private family archive of one woman, Ada Hollis, restored and framed for a home wall and a keepsake folio, not sold to anyone.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Assembled in 2026 at the family house in Vermont, New England, by three siblings in their sixties acting on behalf of twenty two relatives.
brand_identity.about: The archive holds nine photographs of Ada Hollis, who died in April at ninety nine, spanning roughly 1912 to 1974. It exists so that twenty two people who come home at Thanksgiving can hang one wall of her and carry one folio each. The standard is a museum label, not a memory book: honest, quiet, and true to what is actually in the photograph.
brand_identity.audience: Three siblings commissioning on behalf of twenty two family members aged 8 to 74. Not a commercial audience: the work hangs in a family house and is judged by people who knew Ada.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A private heritage commission of 650 to 1,600 dollars. The money buys restraint rather than effect: a true archival neutral, deep honest blacks, one photograph per page, generous margins, and visible respect for the grain and the paper each print is made of.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet text serif set the way a museum sets a wall label: small, calm, well leaded, with a restrained display cut for the folio cover and course of names. Nothing decorative, no script, no drop shadow.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and factual, the voice of a caption card rather than a scrapbook. Example line the brand would write: "Ada Hollis, Brattleboro, 1912. Studio card portrait."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There are no brand files. What survives is nine home flatbed scans, the daughter's catalogue and notes, and the Brattleboro framer's 2019 press PDF for the caption cards, of which six are already on the wall. The framer has retired, so the new cards must match his file rather than a live template.
brand_identity.values: Identity is the whole point: whatever is really in the photograph stays in the photograph, and nothing is invented or tidied away.

assets_supplied.name: hollis_scans/ (9 flatbed scans, approx 2200 x 3000 to 4000 x 5200)
assets_supplied.kind: Home flatbed scans of nine photographs Ada kept, spanning roughly 1912 to 1974: studio card portraits, two mid century black and white prints, and four drugstore colour prints from the sixties and seventies.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Nine photographs of Nan, scanned at home by my brother. Some are faded, some have gone a strange colour, a couple are crooked."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Four of the nine were scanned still inside their album mounts or their deckled paper borders, and in those the picture sits a degree or two off level inside a mount that is itself perfectly square to the scanner glass, so an automatic level locks to the mount edge, reports success, returns a file, and the readout is that nothing has moved. Two of the colour prints have lost most of one dye layer, and which way each one's residual cast runs is not legible while the fade is still on it: the cast only becomes visible once the fade has been lifted and contrast is back, and the two run in opposite directions from each other.

assets_supplied.name: mountcard_2019_print.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The Brattleboro framer's flat press PDF for the caption cards, A6 landscape, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout so it converts cleanly. Carries a title line, a date and place line, a names line, a provenance line in italic, and a small placed reference thumbnail.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card he ran for us in 2019. Six of these are already on the wall and the new ones have to match them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: He drew the caption block around the captions he actually had in 2019, which were two or three words long, and it is a fixed measure frame in a document that does not spill and does not warn: a longer caption simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so a record carrying three names and a place loses its last name and its year at trim while the screen proof still looks like a finished card. What the conversion exposes as addressable structure is a property of how he built that document and is announced nowhere, and the italic provenance line sits as its own run inside a single continuous flow rather than as its own frame.

assets_supplied.name: photo_catalogue.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The spreadsheet Ada's daughter has kept for years, one row per photograph, with columns for caption title, date and place, names, provenance and a photo filename.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What we know about each one. My aunt has kept this list going since the nineties."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two rows are the same photograph, sent to her twice under different filenames by two cousins with slightly different dates, and shipping both puts a duplicate card on a wall that has a fixed number of frames. One row's date contradicts what is written on the back of that print, which appears in the family notes and not in the spreadsheet, and one row's photo column names a file that does not exist anywhere because the family renamed that scan after this export was taken.

assets_supplied.name: family_notes.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Two pages typed by Ada's daughter: what is written on the backs of the prints, who is in each photograph, which town each was taken in, and the things that must not be tidied away.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we know, and the things we do not want touched."

acceptance_bar: The nine restored photographs read as ONE archive hung on one wall: one paper white, one black point, one degree of correction. A photograph that cannot be brought to the set is named to us, not shipped at eighty percent.

Nothing is invented. No detail that is not in the scan appears in the delivery, and nothing that IS in the scan (the scar, the grain, the paper texture, the studio retoucher's original pencil work) is removed because it looked untidy.
Every photograph that is genuinely off level arrives level, and any that could not be levelled without cutting into the picture is named rather than quietly shipped tilted.

No delivered file exceeds its source scan's pixel dimensions and no crop's tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. If a photograph cannot reach the framing size at its own resolution, we are told the size it CAN reach.
Nothing reads as enhanced. A print pushed until it stops looking like a print from its decade fails even if it looks impressive.

Exactly one caption card per catalogued photograph, no duplicate card and no missing card. If the number shipped is not the number the spreadsheet implies, the note says which row was withheld and why.
Every card carries the complete caption for that photograph at TRIM, not merely on a screen proof. A caption that is cut off at the frame edge is a failed card even though the card printed.
Each per-photograph file contains the photograph its filename claims, established by opening it rather than by the order the files came back in.
The proofs are rendered at true print resolution at card trim rather than at screen scale.

The folio comes back as a native editable document we can change ourselves, with every photograph actually visible, the wall plan as a real table, and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own weight.
Anything on the folio cover that is not one of Ada's photographs is honest about being that, and it sits under the restored set rather than against it.

A written note: what was corrected on each photograph and what was deliberately left, every catalogue row questioned and how it was resolved, the type system by role, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (global and masked, including highlight, shadow, temperature and HSL work), image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, upscale_factor and detection_confidence)
adobe_surfaces.role: The restoration itself and the surface the commission is judged on. It levels what is genuinely off level, fixes one archival target and brings nine differently faded photographs from four decades to it one call at a time, triages residual dye casts that run in opposite directions, holds the line between damage and patina, and derives the framing files and the share renditions at native scale while reading the tradeoff record on every call. There is no measurement anywhere in the family, so every judgement here is made by looking at what came back against what went in.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: The caption card run that has to match six cards already hanging. The retired framer's press file becomes a live merge template, the family spreadsheet becomes the data source after reconciliation, and the run produces the cards, the per-photograph single files the family can reprint one at a time, and the proofs. The true story text has to be reconstructed from the exported interchange file rather than trusted from a convenience readout, and the placeholder inventory confirmed by round trip rather than by a success message.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The folio as one native editable document at true physical dimensions: cover, one page per photograph with its caption, the wall plan page, and a share canvas for the family thread. Every photograph inlined as image data because a photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, the wall plan set as a genuine table, family and weight declared per text element, each root declaring its own canvas, and the payload routed by uploaded URL because nine inlined photographs pass the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the folio and the share canvas, and the only place the agent's typographic authorship exists, since no font from this surface can reach the printed caption card. The pairing is the agent's own art direction against a museum label voice rather than a memory book voice, the numeric weight per family is non-standard and cannot be inferred from the style name, one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the honest ground for the folio cover, which cannot be one of Ada's photographs stretched to fill a page and cannot be invented: a licensed, IP clean, camera scale still of aged paper or linen. The Boards half persists the restored set for three siblings in three states to sign off before nine frames are printed, placed within the twelve per call cap with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle the split: caption cards to the merge surface, folio and wall plan to authored canvases, photographs to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: The card is record per page against a layout six existing frames already lock in; the folio is free form and must stay editable, which the merge surface structurally cannot give.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the nine scans, the press PDF, the catalogue and the notes, holding each returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by photograph and by role, because the same scan will exist in four states before the end.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all nine and triage: era, process, what is mount and what is picture, what is damage and what is the age of the thing, how much edge each has to spare.
trajectory.judgement: A studio card portrait from 1912 and a drugstore colour print from 1971 are not the same object and do not want the same instrument. Reading the family notes against each scan is what separates damage from the character the family has asked to keep.
trajectory.produces: A per photograph triage note: process, mount, apparent tilt, fade type, and what must not be touched.

trajectory.action: Level the photographs that sit off square, before any framing crop is derived.
trajectory.judgement: Levelling reframes and eats edge, so it cannot follow the crop. What an automatic level actually took its reference from has to be looked at rather than assumed from the call succeeding.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where levelling worked, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Fix one archival target (one paper white, one black point) and bring each of the nine toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Nine photographs from four decades on four different papers have to arrive at one destination, which means nine different routes rather than one batched move, and the destination itself is a taste decision the family has framed as museum rather than memory book.
trajectory.produces: Nine restored masters at source scale with a per photograph parameter log.

trajectory.action: Recover the fade on the colour prints and neutralise what the recovery reveals, deciding per print how far the correction can go before the print stops looking like a print of its decade.
trajectory.judgement: The residual cast is the whole judgement here, and there is no eyedropper and no histogram anywhere in the connector, so the direction and the size of the correction can only be decided by looking at what came back.
trajectory.produces: Fade recovered, cast corrected colour prints with a record of how far each was taken.

trajectory.action: Lay all nine together in the order the wall will hang them and judge them as one archive rather than as nine restorations.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the set at the only moment the comparison exists, and deciding whether any photograph has been taken far enough that it now reads as enhanced beside its neighbours.
trajectory.produces: A set judged as a set, with any photograph that will not join it named.

trajectory.action: Derive the A4 proportioned framing files and the smaller share renditions, reading confidence and tradeoffs on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: One crop logic across nine, not nine good crops. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop clipped or that an output was interpolated toward the two times cap, which at this band decides whether a photograph can be framed at wall size at all.
trajectory.produces: Framing files and share renditions with their tradeoff records.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the catalogue against the family notes, normalise it into a merge shaped data file with an at prefixed image column holding bare filenames, upload the restored thumbnails and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real reconciliation: one photograph is entered twice, one date is contradicted by the back of the print, and one photo reference points at a file that no longer exists under that name. What is the agent's call and what is the family's to confirm is a decision, and they asked to be told.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, the uploaded card thumbnails, the image map and a list of catalogue questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the press PDF, export the interchange file, unzip it and read the real frame inventory and bounds, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from its concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is a property of the retired framer's document, and every offset must be computed from the document itself rather than from any convenience readout. The thumbnail frame's real bounds have to be read out rather than assumed from how the card looks on the wall.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its interchange export, a frame inventory with real ids and bounds, and a reconstructed story string.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering every copy field plus the thumbnail frame, validate it, prepare the template, then export the interchange file from the RESULT and search for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence, and ordering any rows that share a uid so their positions hold against the original text.
trajectory.produces: A prepared template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with the per row thumbnails bound, then render the card run and the proofs at true print resolution from that document, and produce the per-photograph single files, naming each by opening it.
trajectory.judgement: Merging to the native document first keeps both the press branch and the per-record branch open, and identity by position in a returned list is the fast wrong answer that puts the wrong caption under the wrong photograph.
trajectory.produces: The caption card run, print resolution proofs, and per-photograph files verified by inspection.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered card at trim rather than at proof scale, line by line, against the reconciled catalogue.
trajectory.judgement: A caption that ran past the framer's measure and a wrongly bound thumbnail both look like success at the API boundary, and both look fine on a screen scale proxy.
trajectory.produces: A card by card reconciliation against the catalogue.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the honest cover ground, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the ground whose warmth and whose blacks can live under the restored nine, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale cover ground.

trajectory.action: Bring the licensed ground toward the archive target and lay it under the restored set as the cover will hold it.
trajectory.judgement: Judging the ground against the set at the only moment the comparison is available, and deciding whether it joins, gets pushed further, or gets abandoned for a different search.
trajectory.produces: The cover ground, in or out, with the reasoning recorded.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to answer to a museum label voice rather than a memory book voice. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and actual weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with the A4 folio cover, one page per photograph with its caption, the wall plan page and the share canvas, inline every photograph, set the wall plan as a real table, declare family and weight per text element, then upload it and hold the URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air a museum voice takes and which photograph opens the folio.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the folio, retained as the durable source.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, verify canvas one from the document's rendition and the rest from the returned per canvas markup.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition shows the first artboard only.
trajectory.produces: A native editable folio, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Build the family sign off board within the placement cap, re-sending only entries named as failed, then write the note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success. The note has to say what was corrected and what was deliberately left on each photograph, under the family's own standard about the scar.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the automatic level actually moved the picture. Four of the nine were scanned inside their album mounts or their paper borders, and in those the strongest straight edges in the frame belong to the mount, which is square to the glass, while the photograph sits a degree or two off inside it. The call succeeds, a file comes back, and on those frames it is the file that went in. There is no angle readout, no rotation parameter and no measurement anywhere in the connector, and at thumbnail scale a two degree tilt inside a square mount and a levelled picture look the same, so the only way to learn which frames actually moved is to level them and compare what returned against what went in.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no care prevents it, because the tool takes no options and exposes no reference: what it locked onto is only observable afterwards. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says a couple are crooked and asks for the tilt corrected, which is the client's goal, and no asset note, no deliverable and no earlier step says anything about mounts or borders. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because re-running the same call on the same frame returns the same file. The response is a different instrument and a real decision about how much of the mount is evidence worth keeping.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm the unmoved frames by comparing return against input rather than by trusting the call, then isolate the picture area inside the mount and crop to it before levelling again, decide per photograph whether the deckled border stays as part of the object or goes, and re-derive that photograph's framing crop and its caption card thumbnail from the corrected master.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Four of the nine hang visibly crooked on a wall built for one woman, next to five that are level, in front of twenty two people who asked for exactly this and were told it was done.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which way each faded colour print's residual cast actually runs. Two of the drugstore prints have lost most of one dye layer, and while the fade is still on them both simply read as generically yellowed at any scale: the cast is masked by the missing contrast. Only once the fade is lifted and the tonal range is back does the true bias appear, and on these two it appears in opposite directions, so a neutralisation that visibly rescues one drives the other further off. With no eyedropper and no histogram, the recovery is the diagnostic, and it can only be read by looking at what came back.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it, since the fade must be lifted before the cast is legible, and care cannot settle it, because two prints that look identically yellowed as supplied are not carrying the same fault. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the sixties and seventies prints have gone a strange colour and asks for the colour corrected, which is the goal; no asset note names dye layers or directions. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different correction on one of the two, taken in the opposite direction from the one that worked, and then a fresh judgement of both against the seven others.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Correct each of the two on its own evidence rather than by copying the move that worked, re-judge both against the black and white masters, and decide whether either has been pushed to where it no longer reads as a print of its decade, which the family has ruled out. Any change here re-flows into that photograph's framing file, its share rendition and its card thumbnail.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Half the colour prints on the wall sit visibly green or magenta beside the others, which is precisely the thing the family said was wrong with them in the first place, delivered back as finished restoration work.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every caption actually reaches the printed card. The framer drew the caption block around the captions he had in 2019, which were two or three words, and it is a fixed measure frame: text that runs past it does not spill, does not reflow and does not warn, it simply stops at the frame edge. The merge reports success, the page count equals the row count, the validator was happy and the proof at screen scale reads as a finished card, because a caption that stops after two of three names still looks like a caption. Whether THIS catalogue's longest rows fit THAT frame is a property of the framer's document and cannot be known before the cards are rendered at trim and read.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it and nothing in the merge chain reports overset, so an agent doing everything correctly still cannot learn it before rendering. (b) Nothing states it. The brief asks for one card per photograph matching the 2019 set, which is the goal, and the acceptance line about complete captions is the family's own standing requirement, not a disclosure that a specific record overflows. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is an editorial and typographic decision (shorten the caption, split the names onto the line the framer left for them, or accept a smaller size on one line) taken against six cards already hanging that cannot be changed.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every rendered card at trim rather than at proof scale, identify which records are losing content, then re-cut those captions or re-assign content between the framer's existing lines so nothing is lost, re-merge, re-render and re-read, and record in the note which caption wording was changed and why so the family is not surprised by it on the wall.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A card goes into a frame beside six from 2019 with a woman's married name and the year simply missing, printed, mounted and hung, discovered by the family at Thanksgiving rather than by us.

deliverables.name: Ada Hollis restored archive, nine photographs plus one licensed cover ground
deliverables.spec: Nine photographs from four decades brought to one archival target (one paper white, one black point, one degree of correction, one crop logic), levelled where levelling is honest, fade recovered and cast corrected where the print has actually shifted, with nothing invented and nothing that is genuinely in the scan removed. Delivered as A4 proportioned framing files and smaller share renditions, every output at or below its source dimensions, plus one licensed camera scale cover ground graded into the same set, with a per photograph parameter log and one line on why each differs.

deliverables.name: Caption card run, press cards plus per-photograph files and proofs
deliverables.spec: One A6 caption card per catalogued photograph, card count equal to the reconciled catalogue, each binding the title, the date and place, the names and the provenance verbatim and complete at trim, plus that photograph's own restored thumbnail. Accompanied by one single card file per photograph, named to the photograph and identity verified by opening it, and by proofs rendered at true print resolution from the merged document. Produced by reverse engineering a retired framer's press file into a live merge template, so the template and the record of how it was derived are handed back.

deliverables.name: Thanksgiving folio and wall plan as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable document carrying the A4 folio cover, one page per photograph with its caption, the wall plan page and the share canvas, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the wall plan as a genuine table, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, so the family can add the three more names the aunt will find and the folio survives regardless of the document's retention.

deliverables.name: Restoration note and family sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was corrected on each photograph and what was deliberately left and why, any photograph that could not be levelled or could not reach framing size at its own resolution, every catalogue row questioned and how it was resolved, any caption wording changed to fit the framer's card and the reason, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the restored set for three siblings in three states to sign off before nine frames are printed.

verifiers_auto.text: The caption card run has exactly one page per reconciled catalogue row.
verifiers_auto.how: Count pages in the merged press output and compare against the normalised data file row count.

verifiers_auto.text: Every copy field exists as a placeholder in the prepared template before any merge.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the interchange file from the prepared template, unzip it and search the stories for each field token.

verifiers_auto.text: Each per-photograph file contains the photograph its filename claims.
verifiers_auto.how: Open every per-photograph file and read its title and names fields against the filename.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given six cards already hanging that cannot change and a folio the family will keep editing.
What is damage to correct and what is the age of the object to preserve, on prints where grain, paper texture and a studio retoucher's pencil work are all present.
Whether an automatic level actually moved a given picture, and how much of an album mount or a deckled border is evidence worth keeping when it did not.
Which way each faded colour print's residual cast runs, when both read identically yellowed as supplied and no measurement exists anywhere.
How far a fade recovery can be taken before the print stops looking like a print of its decade, at a band where anything that reads as enhanced fails.
One archival target for four decades and four papers, and which photograph, if any, cannot be brought to it.
The catalogue: one photograph entered twice, one date contradicted by the back of the print, one photo reference pointing at a renamed file. What is the agent's call and what is the family's.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the framer's text or to reconstruct the story independently from the document.
Whether per-photograph identity is established by position in a returned list or by opening the file.
What to do with a caption that will not fit the framer's measure, when six cards from 2019 fix the design and the family asked for a match.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a museum label voice rather than a memory book voice.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the scans into a frontier image model and it returns a beautiful old photograph of a woman who is not Ada Hollis. IDENTITY is the entire commission: a generative restore invents the eyes, the hairline, the teeth and the hand, and this family has already told us in writing what happened the last time somebody improved their grandmother. Every corrected pixel must derive from the pixels in the scan. SPEC: the family needs one A6 caption card per catalogued photograph matching six already hanging, complete at trim, with per-photograph files each containing the photograph they claim, and proofs at true print resolution. EDITABILITY: the folio is defined by being editable, because the aunt will find three more names. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this level actually move the picture, which way does this cast run once the fade is lifted, does this caption reach the edge of the card.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments global and masked, monochromatic_tint, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor are all verified headless. The two imaging checkpoints rest on documented facts rather than invention: there is NO measurement anywhere in the family (no eyedropper, no histogram, no ruler, and metadata.bbox is a mask extent, not a tonal or angular reading), and image_auto_straighten takes no reference and reports no angle, so what it locked onto and whether it moved anything can only be established by comparing the returned file against the input. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating up to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, which is what makes the no enlargement bar checkable rather than asserted. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified, one record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, per-record files are confirmed in correct order by two routes, true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool, the merge's own resolution parameter is documented as silently ignored (hence rendering from the merged document), frame granularity and frame bounds from a PDF are documented as not under your control, and the mapping readout's text content is documented as lossy in a way the validator blesses. The caption checkpoint needs no new capability: the converted document carries the bounds the framer drew, nothing in the chain reports overset, and text past a fixed measure is simply absent from the render while the page count stays correct. Image binding through an at prefixed column plus an image map is verified, with the single-record loop as the identity guaranteed fallback. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, true mm print canvases at exactly 96 dpi, real tables and a genuine editable document are verified; the rendition shows PAGE 1 ONLY so verification splits between the rendition and the returned markup; payload routed by uploaded URL because inlined photographs pass 70KB immediately. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS follow the verified chains, with short queries, orientation never passed, and the twelve per call board cap with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no generative fill or AI restore, no healing or cloning, no sharpening, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no batch above 20.
